name: Queen's Slipper 500
description: Queen's Slipper 500 is the definitive Australian version of the card game 500, played using specialized decks produced by the iconic Queen's Slipper brand. While standard 500 exists, the Australian variant is unique for its use of 11s, 12s, and 13s, allowing for 4, 5, or even 6-player games with expanded decks. It is a trick-taking game that evolved from Euchre, featuring a complex bidding system, the 'MisÃ¨re' (no-trick) contract, and the inclusion of a Joker as the ultimate trump card.

history.origins: Originally created in the US in 1904 by the US Playing Card Co. It spread to Australia where the 'Queen's Slipper' brand popularized a variant with expanded suit counts and the MisÃ¨re bid.
timeline: 1904: USPC Co copyrights the original 500 rules.
1920s: Gathers immense popularity in Australia, becoming the national social game.
1960s: Queen's Slipper brand (Lenz) standardizes the '500's Deck' with 11s, 12s, and 13s.
Present: Remains a core cultural institution in Australian community centers, schools, and homes.
history.cultural: Commonly played as a 'Pub Game' and in formal 500 clubs across Melbourne and regional Victoria.
history.evolution: The game moved from a 10-trick structure to include high-stakes 'Kitty' swaps and the famous 'Double MisÃ¨re' variants.

setup.deck: 43 cards for a 4-handed game: 4s to Aces, plus the Joker and the 11s/12s of specific suits (depends on house rules).
setup.dealing: 3 cards, 1 to kitty, 4 cards, 1 to kitty, 3 cards, 1 to kitty (Total: 10 cards each, 3 in kitty).

rules.objective: Be the first team to reach 500 points or force opponents to -500 points.
rules.gameplay: Partners sit opposite. Deal 10 each and 3 to kitty. Bid from six tricks in a suit or No Trumps, or Misere (lose every trick) or Open Misere. Highest bidder takes kitty, discards three, and leads. Follow suit; trick to highest trump or highest of led suit. Joker is highest trump; Right and Left Bower next. First team to 500 wins; minus 500 loses.
keyRules: Bidding order: Spades lowest, Clubs, Diamonds, Hearts, No Trumps. Misere only after someone bid seven. Contractor picks up kitty and discards three. Must follow suit. Trick winner leads next. Opponents score 10 per trick taken when contractors make contract.

strategy.basic: Count your Bowers! The Jack of the trump suit (Right) and its same-colored brother (Left) are more powerful than the Ace. If you hold the Joker and both Bowers, you possess the 'The Nuts'â€”you can lead with them to clear all other trumps from the table. Don't bid heavily if you only have high Aces; you can easily be blocked by the Jacks.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Kitty' Discard: After you win the bid and take the Kitty, you must discard three cards. Don't just discard your lowest cards. If you have only one card of a specific suit (a 'Singleton'), discard it! This allows you to trump that suit the first time it is led, gaining a trick you would have otherwise lost.
strategy.advanced: MisÃ¨re Defense: If an opponent bids MisÃ¨re, your team must work together to 'Force' them to win a trick. Lead suits where you have many low cards. If you see the MisÃ¨re player stalling on a suit (e.g., they play a 7 when you lead a 4), they are afraid of that suit. Lead it again! Defense against MisÃ¨re is about 'Hand-Squeezing' the bidder until they have no choice but to take a trick.
tips: A 'Seven Spades' bid is the lowest possible. It's often used just to see of your partner has anything.
The Joker is worth 0 in No Trump if led, but is still the highest cardâ€”remember the No Trump special rules.

variations.name: Joker in No Trumps
variations.description: Some play that in No Trumps the joker cannot be nominated in advance as belonging to a suit; or that the joker cannot be played on a lead of a suit on which you have previously reneged.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: House-rule variant; engine overrides not yet mapped for joker nomination rules.

variations.name: Bidding process
variations.description: Some allow bidding after pass (auction continues until three passes in succession). Some allow the contractor to raise the final bid after everyone has passed.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Auction timing variant; overrides for bid-after-pass need further source lookup.

variations.name: Misere ranking and scoring
variations.description: House rules vary: Misere allowed only after a seven bid; Open Misere ranking between 9 No Trumps and 10 Spades or as highest; alternative scores (e.g. Misere 150, Open Misere 250, misere without pickup 350).
